Right, let me dictate this before I forget it. Three blocks. First: as per our call, here is what was agreed. Second, on our side: the revised proposal will be sent by Wednesday, including the four-week timeline and one clarification on late data. Third, on their side: the employee file needs to be sent to us by Friday. Then the open point. Careful here. Do not write you have not approved the budget, that sounds like blame. Write: the budget has not been approved yet. And one last line, and this one stays active on purpose, because the credit is ours: we completed the last onboarding of this size two days early.

I got their email on Tuesday. Three paragraphs, very polite, and I read it twice without understanding what I was supposed to do. There were no dates in it. It said things were being progressed and that they remained at my disposal. At my disposal for what? So I had to call them to ask, which is precisely what the email was supposed to save me from. Look, I do not need it to be beautiful. I need three things: names, dates, and one line telling me what I have to do. If it has those, I can act on it in thirty seconds and get on with my day.
